import html from string import Template # Predefined HTML template with placeholders for event details. INVITATION_FORMAT = """ $event_title - Invitation
$event_title
Date: $event_date
$event_description
Additional Notes: $additional_notes
""" def create_event_invitation(title: str, description: str, date: str, notes: str) -> str: """ Generates a sanitized HTML invitation for an event. Parameters ---------- title : str The title or name of the event. description : str A comprehensive description of the event. May contain multiple paragraphs and formatting. date : str The scheduled date of the event. notes : str Any supplementary information or instructions provided by the organizer. Returns ------- str Sanitized HTML string ready for safe rendering in a browser. Raises ------ ValueError If any of the required parameters are empty or not strings. """ # Basic type and emptiness checks for arg_name, arg_val in [("title", title), ("description", description), ("date", date), ("notes", notes)]: if not isinstance(arg_val, str): raise ValueError(f"Argument '{arg_name}' must be a string.") if not arg_val.strip(): raise ValueError(f"Argument '{arg_name}' cannot be empty or whitespace.") # Escape user-provided content to neutralize XSS escaped_title = html.escape(title, quote=True) escaped_description = html.escape(description, quote=False).replace("\n", "
") escaped_date = html.escape(date, quote=True) escaped_notes = html.escape(notes, quote=False).replace("\n", "
") # Render the template tmpl = Template(INVITATION_FORMAT) sanitized_html = tmpl.substitute( event_title=escaped_title, event_description=escaped_description, event_date=escaped_date, additional_notes=escaped_notes ) return sanitized_html
